newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia declares moratorium on death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Georgia declares moratorium on death penalty.

text.p: Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze declared a moratorium on the death penalty on Tuesday ahead of planned changes in the Caucasian republic's penal code.
Shevardnadze, a former Soviet foreign minister, announced the moratorium in a message sent to the country's parliament and coincided with International Human Rights Day.
However under the planned revisions, which come into effect next February, capital punishment will still be imposed for premeditated murder.
Other crimes that currently merit the death penalty, including treason, will be punished by life imprisonment.
Georgia was one of many former Soviet republics criticised on Tuesday by the U.S.-based Human Rights Watch/Helsinki over its human rights record.
